How SIMPLE SEQUEL works

1. Import

Drop one or many files on the panel at the left, or click it to browse. Every file becomes a table. Workbooks with several sheets become one table per sheet. Supported: .xlsx .xlsm .xlsb .xls .ods .csv .tsv .txt .json .jsonl .ndjson .html .xml, plus anything that is really one of those underneath.

Rename a table by typing in its name box. The SQL name underneath (for example sales_2024) is what you use in a query, and clicking it copies it. If your first row is not a header, use the H button on the table card to promote or demote it.

2. Query

The full SQLite dialect is available: joins, CTEs, window functions, GROUP BY, CASE, date functions, and so on. Each run adds a new result table, so you can keep several side by side.

Name a result on the way out with a leading comment: -- name: revenue_by_city. Use Ctrl + Enter to run.

3. Edit the result

  • Edit a cell: click it and type. Changes save as you go. Clearing a cell leaves it empty (NULL), not the text "null".
  • Sort: click a column header. First click sorts ascending, second descending, third clears it. Blanks always sort to the bottom.
  • Filter by value: the ▽ on a column header lists every distinct value in that column with its row count. Click a value to see only that value, then keep clicking to add more in one go: the list stays open and shows how many rows are left. Click a chosen value again to drop it. Show all clears the filter, and (Blanks) finds the empty cells. Type in the box to find a value, and press Enter to use everything that matches. Column filters and the text search combine.
  • Filter by text: type in the search box. Separate words to require all of them, or use column:value to target one column.
  • Reorder: drag the grip handle on the left of a row, or use the ↑ ↓ buttons.
  • Delete: the ✕ on the row.
  • Add: the Add row button under the grid.
  • Undo an edit session: press Revert in the result footer.

4. Download

Each result table downloads as CSV, Excel or JSON. Download opens a picker where you choose any number of result tables and get them as a ZIP, or one file at a time. Downloads carry the sorted order you see; filters apply only when you tick export visible rows only.

Source tables download too, from the small download button on each card.

Good to know

  • Nothing leaves this browser tab. There is no server, no account and no telemetry, so it works offline once saved.
  • Reloading the page clears the session, so download what you need first. Keep the file itself somewhere safe.
  • Cell edits and row changes live in the result table only. Re-running the query builds a fresh result.
  • Empty spreadsheet cells are imported as true NULLs, so WHERE col IS NULL and IS NOT NULL work as you would expect. A cell that literally contains the word null stays text.
  • Very large files: parsing is in memory, so keep an eye on files above roughly 50 MB.
